articles.title: Horizontal film or vertical reel: which listing video does your property need?
articles.summary: What each format is for, where it plays, and when a listing is worth both.
articles.answer: Choose horizontal film when the video will live on the listing page, YouTube, email and your listing presentations. Choose a vertical reel when the launch runs mainly on Instagram, TikTok and Reels. When a property will be marketed on both, plan both formats from the same shoot rather than cropping one into the other.

p: A horizontal (16:9) film is built for screens people watch deliberately: the listing page, YouTube, an email campaign, a presentation to sellers. It has room for the full width of a room, the relationship between spaces and the setting around the house.
It suits properties where the story of the property depends on flow and scale: open plans, long sightlines, water, land.
A vertical (9:16) reel is made for the phone feed. It is shorter, faster and framed for one subject at a time: the entry, the kitchen island, the view from the primary suite.
It is the better choice when the launch is led by social channels, and it is included in the Social Media package for that reason.

sections.h: Why we shoot both formats on purpose
p: Cropping a horizontal film into a vertical one loses the edges of every frame, and a vertical shot stretched to horizontal looks like what it is. When both formats are needed, we plan and capture each one deliberately on the same visit.

list: Listing Starter: photography, drone and floor plan, no video.
Social Media: vertical cinematic reel (with photography and drone).
Luxury Media and Signature: both the horizontal film and the vertical reel.
On their own: a single cinematic video or reel, or both from the same shoot, priced by square footage.
sections.note: Prices change with property size. The pricing page shows the exact amount for your square footage.

list: Where will buyers and sellers actually see it? Listing page and presentations point to horizontal; a social-first launch points to vertical.
Is the property's appeal in its scale and setting, or in a few standout moments? Scale favors horizontal; moments suit a reel.
Will you also use the listing to market yourself? Both formats give you more to share after the sale.

articles.title: When do twilight, drone and a floor plan add value to a listing?
articles.summary: What each one shows buyers that standard daytime photos cannot, and when to skip it.
articles.answer: Add drone when the land, water, neighborhood or the way the home sits on its lot is part of the value. Add twilight when the home has lighting, architecture or outdoor spaces that come alive at dusk. Add a floor plan for almost any listing where buyers need to understand the layout before they visit.

sections.h: Drone: context a ground photo cannot give
p: Aerials show what a ground photo cannot: the water, the land, the neighborhood and how the home sits in it. On the East End that is often a large part of what a buyer is paying for.
It adds less when the lot is tight, the surroundings do not help the story, or local rules and weather limit the flight.

sections.h: Twilight: the evening version of the home
p: Twilight stills photograph the home at dusk with interior and landscape lighting on. They carry the presentation into the evening and can lead a listing launch.
They suit homes with strong architecture, pools, terraces and designed lighting. A home with little exterior lighting or a plain facade gains less.

sections.h: Floor plan: understanding the layout before the visit
p: A schematic floor plan lets buyers understand the layout before they visit, so the people who book showings arrive better prepared. It is useful for most listings, and especially for larger or unusual layouts that photos alone cannot explain.

list: Drone photography is included in every listing package.
A schematic floor plan is included in Listing Starter, Luxury Media and Signature.
Twilight photography and day-to-night film are included in Signature, and twilight is also available on its own.
Each is also available on its own or as an add-on; the pricing page shows current prices by property size.
